title: Console first screen: the eager JS closure (1.95 MB, same 120 chunks on every page) is ~2 s of LCP; slim what the shell imports eagerly
body:
repo:objectstack#2 · os-sales · session_01L6bhgV6i8jfWwSXjpWJrjA

Filing gate: maintainer ruling on #37444 at 2026-11-26 13:43Z (「先做最小一刀,其余立卡排队」: slice C rides #37444, the other seams queue as their own cards) · Source: fleet (production re-measure on #37444, comment 7193730951)

## What happens

Reading on a production build (objectstack `021524cd`, brotli on, Lighthouse 13.6.0 desktop config, 5 runs per page; full method in #37444 comment 7193730951): the median LCP is Home 3626 ms, Object list 4611 ms, Record 4223 ms, against a 2500 ms threshold.

Bytes are about 2 s of every page. 2.2–2.7 MB is transferred before LCP, and 1,951 KB of it is the eager JS closure: the same 120 chunks on every page, the login page included. The largest eager chunks (gzip) are vendor-objectstack 684 KB (`@objectstack/spec` zod modules for view/dashboard/object/flow/action, plus formula and client), ui-components 351 KB, index 131 KB, framework 89 KB, vendor-react 80 KB, i18n-locale-en 71 KB and vendor-radix 58 KB. With bandwidth unlimited (RTT 40) the pages drop to 1.7 / 2.4 / 2.1 s.

A probe build that marked zod builder calls pure (`treeshake.manualPureFunctions: ['z']`) saved only 13 KB. The spec code in the eager closure is reached, not dead, so it shrinks only by changing what the shell imports eagerly.

## Expected

- The console shell's eager closure no longer pulls the spec schema modules (and other route-only code) that the first screen doesn't need; they load with the route or feature that uses them.
- Lower the console eager-closure budget the build already checks (see #34927, #26131) to the new size, so the closure can't grow back unseen.
- Re-measure the three pages with the #37444 method and record the new medians on that card.

Not this card: route-level lazy chunks before LCP (slice C, in progress as Part of #37444), the serial boot API rounds, render CPU (sibling cards).

Related: #37444, #37398.

Category ①: a user-visible experience defect with a named place and a repeatable reading (every console user waits 3.6–4.6 s on the first screen).
Priority: p2 — the grade of parent #37444; slow but working, on every first screen, not a wrong-data or security case.
Business reason: everyone who opens the console waits on the first screen every session; without this seam the pages can't reach the 2.5 s threshold #37444 sets.
Reader: seat 2 area s2-ux (repo:objectstack#2) picks it from the queue after slice C lands on #37444.
Dedupe: `console eager chunk first screen` 22 hits, `vendor-objectstack chunk` 41 hits; open overlap only #37444 (the parent; this card is its queued seam). Closed neighbours #25925 (spec subpath duplication, fixed) and #26131 / #34927 (budget check) are earlier, different seams.
